sectors.name: Financials
themes: Digital lending and fintech penetration in Indonesia is accelerating as bank credit growth outpaces GDP, driven by rising middle-class consumption and regulatory support for alternative credit scoring

US financials face headwinds from delayed Fed cuts and tighter commercial real estate exposure, making Indonesian financials a relative safe-haven for regional capital flows.
sectors.ai: Expect continued selective strength in Indonesian financials, led by digital-lending and fintech names (FUJI, BSWD, COIN) as retail credit demand rebounds and regulatory tailwinds favor formalization. Rotate into high-beta small caps with earnings momentum, but trim exposure to US-listed financials where rate-cut repricing caps upside. Maintain overweight on ID financials, targeting 8-12% alpha over 3 months.

sectors.name: Mining & Energy
themes: Indonesia's mandatory domestic processing (smelter) policy continues to structurally re-rate nickel and downstream metals names, favoring integrated players with captive ore supply.
Global gold price strength, driven by central bank buying and geopolitical hedging, provides durable tailwinds for Indonesian gold miners with expanding production profiles.
Coal's rally is fragile amid China's import normalization and domestic DMO price caps, making it a tactical trade rather than a structural hold.
sectors.ai: Buy selective exposure to nickel and gold names (MBMA, BRMS, AMMN) as Indonesia's downstream processing push and global gold strength persist; avoid chasing coal (COAL, SGER) given policy and price volatility. Position for Q3 earnings catalysts and rupiah stability, with ALKA/PSAB momentum likely short-lived.

sectors.name: Renewables & Climate-Tech
themes: US solar and storage names are re-rating on falling rate expectations and IRA implementation clarity, creating durable upside for inverter and residential installers through 2025.
Indonesia's EV value chain is structurally accelerating via nickel downstreaming and domestic content rules, making VKTR and TOBA core beneficiaries of local manufacturing mandates.
Power utilities (NRG, CEG) are gaining defensive bid as AI-driven electricity demand forecasts tighten supply, supporting long-term contracted cash flows despite near-term volatility.
sectors.ai: Buy pullbacks in US-listed solar/energy storage names (SEDG, ENPH, RUN) and Indonesia EV/battery plays (VKTR, TOBA) on strength; sector breadth is healthy with normal signals and US leadership. Trim NRG/CEG only if utilities decouple from rate-cut expectations. Prioritize VKTR for domestic EV adoption catalysts and SEDG for US policy tailwinds into Q3.

sectors.name: Consumer & FMCG
themes: Rural consumption is accelerating as staple volume growth outpaces urban, favoring distributors with deep Java and Sumatra networks.
Commodity-linked FMCG players (palm, agar, poultry) are capturing margin expansion from softer input costs, a structural tailwind into 2026.
Digital-first consumer brands are disrupting legacy channels, with e-commerce and social commerce driving faster SKU velocity and repeat purchase rates.
sectors.ai: Buy consumer names with direct commodity exposure and digital distribution; BRRC, COIN, and JARR are leading on volume-driven repricing, not just sentiment. Rotate into mid-cap FMCG with rural penetration upside, as IDX consumer breadth confirms durable demand recovery. Trim laggards lacking pricing power, and add on any pullback to 10-day support.

sectors.name: Logistics
themes: Indonesia's domestic logistics demand is structurally rising with e-commerce penetration and island-to-island distribution networks, favoring local operators over global freight names.

Consolidation in fragmented trucking and warehousing segments is accelerating, with small caps like TRUK and TAMU gaining share via digital freight matching and regional hubs.
sectors.ai: Logistics upside is broadening beyond port plays into mid-cap movers (TRUK, LOPI, TAMU) on domestic trade resilience and e-commerce parcel growth; add exposure to last-mile and cold-chain names, rotate out of US-linked freight laggards. Near-term catalyst: Q3 volume data and fuel subsidy adjustments.
